title: Serving in production: Gunicorn, Uvicorn and a reverse proxy

videos.script: runserver has warned you since lesson 2. It is not for production. Today, agenda moves to the setup a server runs. {{title}} Gunicorn runs Django in three worker processes. Kill one, and the master starts another at once. Uvicorn does the same for the API. {{workers}} Then systemd. Every process gets a unit, starts at boot, and comes back when it dies. The secrets sit in a file only root can read. {{systemd}} nginx goes in front of both applications. It serves the static files from disk, adds the headers FastAPI does not, and passes the rest along. {{nginx}} With a certificate, port 80 only redirects, and Django's last four HTTPS warnings are gone. {{https}} Behind a proxy, every request seems to come from the proxy. Two headers say otherwise, and you see a forged address ignored. {{forwarded}} Last, three failures: a 502 when the application is down, a configuration that does not parse, and a redirect that never ends.
